examples.en: A tasty smell is making my mouth water.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 제 구미에 딱 맞아요.
examples.en: This movie is exactly to my taste.

examples.ko: 아이들 구미에 맞게 음식을 순하게 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made the food mild to suit the kids' tastes.

examples.ko: 그 회사 일은 월급이 많아서 구미가 당겨요.
examples.en: That job is tempting because the pay is high.

examples.ko: 어려운 책은 제 구미에 안 맞아요.
examples.en: Difficult books aren't to my liking.

examples.ko: 광고는 손님의 구미를 당기려고 사진을 크게 보여 줘요.
examples.en: Ads show big photos to whet customers' appetite.

explain: 입맛이라는 뜻이지만 대부분 '구미가 당기다', '구미에 맞다'로만 나와요. 음식 이야기에는 '입맛'이나 '식욕'이 더 자연스러워요. 일이나 제안에 마음이 끌릴 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 제안이 구미가 당겨서 한번 생각해 볼게요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식뿐 아니라 일이나 제안에 마음이 끌릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for food, but also when a job or offer catches your interest.

explain_en: It originally refers to appetite, but it almost always appears in set patterns like 구미가 당기다 and 구미에 맞다. For plain food talk, 입맛 or 식욕 sounds more natural. It also covers being drawn to a job or offer.

examples.en: The family gathers to make winter kimchi.
This weekend we made winter kimchi at Grandma's house.

examples.ko: 올해는 배추 오십 포기로 김장할 거예요.
examples.en: This year I'll make winter kimchi with fifty heads of cabbage.
On kimjang day, we eat boiled pork.

examples.ko: 요즘은 김장하지 않고 사 먹는 집도 많아요.
examples.en: These days many households buy kimchi instead of making it.

examples.ko: 어머니와 같이 김장하는 게 힘들지만 즐거워요.
examples.en: Making winter kimchi with my mother is tiring but fun.

explain: 그냥 김치를 담글 때는 '김치를 담그다'라고 하고, 늦가을에 겨울 동안 먹을 김치를 한꺼번에 많이 담글 때만 '김장하다'라고 해요. 이웃과 나눠 먹는 한국의 김장 문화는 유네스코 무형유산이에요.
explain_en: Making ordinary kimchi is '김치를 담그다'; '김장하다' is only for making a large batch in late autumn to last the winter. Korea's kimjang culture of sharing with neighbors is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.

examples.en: Neobiani was served on the feast table.
I could smell my mother grilling neobiani.

examples.ko: 이 한식 도시락에는 너비아니가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This Korean lunch box has neobiani in it.
The kids like neobiani the most.
Neobiani and rice alone make a filling meal.
For lunch today I'll have the neobiani set meal.

explain: 양념한 소고기를 넓적하게 저며 구운 한국 음식이에요. 불고기와 비슷하다고 생각하는 사람이 많지만, 잔치나 도시락 반찬처럼 한 점씩 집어 먹는 구이로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a Korean dish of seasoned beef cut into broad slices and grilled. Many people think of it as similar to bulgogi, but it often appears as a grilled side dish eaten piece by piece, as at feasts or in lunch boxes.

en: particularly good taste; food with particularly good taste

examples.en: In this region, oyster pancakes are the winter specialty.
Cold noodles are a summer treat.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 김치전은 최고의 별미 같아요.
examples.en: On a rainy day, kimchi pancakes feel like the best treat.

examples.ko: 여행 가면 그 지역 별미를 꼭 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: When I travel, I always try the local specialty.
Even cup noodles are a treat when I eat them once in a while.

examples.ko: 별미로 먹는 간식이라 평소엔 안 만들어요.
examples.en: It's a snack for special occasions, so I don't usually make it.

explain: 평소에 먹는 밥이 아니라 특별히 맛있게 느껴지는 음식에 써요. 그 계절이나 그 지역에서만 맛볼 수 있는 음식에도 자주 써요. '별식'(특별한 음식)과도 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to food that tastes especially good compared with everyday meals, and it is often used for seasonal or regional dishes. It is close in meaning to '별식' (a special dish).

examples.ko: 싼 게 비지떡이라더니 가방이 금방 망가졌어요.
examples.en: They say cheap things are no good, and sure enough the bag broke quickly.
The bijitteok my grandmother made for me was warm.
I bought bijitteok at the market and ate it as a snack.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 비지떡을 자주 먹었다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: He said he often ate bijitteok when he was little.

examples.ko: 비지떡 한 조각에 따뜻한 차를 마셨어요.
examples.en: I had a piece of bijitteok with a cup of hot tea.
I bought it because it was cheap, but it was worthless.

explain: 음식 이름이지만 속담 '싼 게 비지떡'으로도 알려져 있어요. 값싼 물건을 샀다가 품질이 나빠 후회할 때 '비지떡이었다'처럼 비유로 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 싼 게 비지떡이라고 하잖아요. 너무 싼 물건은 조심하세요.
phrases.en: They say you get what you pay for. Be careful with things that are too cheap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 싼 물건은 품질도 그만큼 떨어진다는 뜻의 속담이에요. 싼 물건을 샀다가 실망했을 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that cheap goods tend to be low in quality. People often say it when disappointed after buying something cheap.
phrases.en_equiv: you get what you pay for

explain_en: It is the name of a food, but it is also known through the proverb '싼 게 비지떡'. When you buy something cheap and regret its poor quality, you can say '비지떡이었다' figuratively.

examples.en: On cold days I crave a hot bowl of seonjitguk.

examples.ko: 이 식당 선짓국은 국물이 진하고 맛있어요.
examples.en: The seonjitguk at this restaurant has a rich, tasty broth.
I put rice in the seonjitguk and ate it.
I miss the seonjitguk my mother used to cook.
It's my first time having seonjitguk, but it's surprisingly good.
I ordered a bowl of seonjitguk and some kimchi.

explain: 소의 피를 굳힌 '선지'를 넣고 끓인 국이에요. 처음 먹는 사람은 호불호가 갈려요. 식당에서는 '선지국'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a soup made with '선지', congealed beef blood. People who try it for the first time often either love it or dislike it. At restaurants it is also called '선지국'.

examples.en: I tried sea urchin seaweed soup in Jeju.

examples.ko: 성게는 가시가 많아서 조심해서 만져야 해요.
examples.en: Sea urchins have many spines, so you must touch them carefully.
I saw a person catching sea urchins at the beach.
This sea urchin roe is nutty and sweet, so it's delicious.
A sea urchin is stuck between the rocks.
This restaurant is famous for its sea urchin bibimbap.

explain: 먹는 부분은 '성게알'이라고 불러서 메뉴에는 '성게알'이라고 적힌 경우도 많아요. 가시가 있는 바다 동물이라 바닷가에서 만지면 위험할 수 있어요.
explain_en: The edible part is called '성게알' (sea urchin roe), so menus often use that word. It is a spiny sea animal, so touching one at the beach can be dangerous.

examples.en: After drinking cold omija tea, my thirst went away.

examples.ko: 오미자는 여러 가지 맛이 다 난다고 해요.
examples.en: They say omija has several different tastes all at once.

examples.ko: 시골 할머니가 오미자를 말려서 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother in the countryside dried omija and sent it to me.

examples.ko: 여름에는 오미자 화채를 자주 만들어 먹어요.
examples.en: In summer I often make and eat omija punch.

examples.ko: 가을에는 시장에 빨간 오미자가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: In autumn, lots of red omija show up at the market.

examples.ko: 오미자에 꿀을 넣어서 차게 마셔 봤어요.
examples.en: I put honey in omija and drank it cold.

explain: 열매 이름이고 '오미자차', '오미자청'처럼 음료로 많이 먹어요. 한자로는 다섯 가지 맛(五味)이라는 뜻이라서 맛이 여러 가지라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the name of a berry and is often enjoyed as a drink, such as '오미자차' or '오미자청'. In Chinese characters it means 'five flavors' (五味), which is why people say it tastes of several things at once.

examples.en: The child crunches away on a cucumber.

examples.ko: 형이 과자를 우적우적 먹으면서 영화를 봐요.
examples.en: My brother watches a movie while munching on snacks.
The horse is chomping on grass.
I was so hungry that I wolfed down the bread.
If you crunch ice, your teeth hurt.
He took a big crunchy bite of the apple.

explain: 단단하거나 질긴 것을 거칠게 씹는 소리와 모양에 써요. '아삭아삭'은 신선한 채소나 과일의 가벼운 식감이고, '우물우물'은 입 안에서 천천히 씹는 모양이라 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It describes the sound and look of chewing hard or tough food roughly. '아삭아삭' is the light crispness of fresh vegetables or fruit, and '우물우물' is slow chewing in the mouth, so they differ.
